Earlier this year, rumours were swirling about a brand-new Health app coming with iOS 26.4. The project was then delayed, iOS 27 has been out for a while now, and still no sign of this revamp.

With the new generation of Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to debut next month, one can't help but ask: will these new features arrive alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's worth looking back at why these features are very likely to arrive in September. You might be thinking: "Shouldn't all software be released in June?" But there is in fact precedent.

watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnoea detection, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications — none of these required the latest hardware, yet all were held back for September.

For these reasons, there's a strong chance Apple will wait until September to unveil the latest Health app upgrade, even though these features may not require a brand-new Apple Watch to function.

There's still time

Ahead of WWDC27, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman warned that the Health app upgrade, codenamed "Project Mulberry", might not appear at the WWDC keynote. As it turned out, his prediction was correct:

Does this mean Project Mulberry is definitely coming at the September keynote? Not necessarily. However, given the multiple precedents of features being announced in September, and knowing it was likely to come later than WWDC anyway, a September debut looks quite probable — even if it ultimately has to wait until October to launch properly with iOS 27.1.

Feature recap

With so many variables at play, the rumours around this suite of features have been flip-flopping constantly. You may have heard that one rumour was a standalone Health+ subscription service featuring videos from doctors. However, reports indicate that plan has been scaled back, with the features instead being integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two things are already very clear: first, an AI health coach will be launched, providing health advice based on your Health app data; second, the ability to give you real-time guidance on exercise and other health-related tasks via your camera. Additionally, another focus of this upgrade is a brand-new Health app design that makes data more immediately visible.

Beyond that, all we can do is wait and see. Personally, I'm very much looking forward to having a better way to organise and understand my own Apple health data.
